summary: LEAD reads a value from a later row in the same ordered partition without a self join.
syntax: LEAD(value, offset, default) OVER (PARTITION BY group_key ORDER BY sequence)
documentation: LEAD reads a value from a later row in the same ordered partition without a self join. The default offset is one. Its default argument is used when that row does not exist, not when an existing next row contains NULL.
inputs: readings(id INTEGER, device TEXT, value INTEGER).
returns: id, device and next_value, ordered by device then id.
caution: Order must be deterministic. A default of -1 is only a missing-next-row marker here; stored NULL values remain NULL.
scenarios: Compare a device reading with its next observation.
Preview the next scheduled item within each team.
Measure gaps between adjacent imported events.
title: Look ahead within each device
problem: Return id, device, LEAD(value,1,-1) OVER (PARTITION BY device ORDER BY id) AS next_value, ordered by device, id. Preserve NULL in an existing next row.
goal: Use LEAD() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Partition by device; the default belongs inside LEAD.
